html:
The Convention for the Extension of Hong Kong Territory, signed in Beijing on 9 June 1898, leased the New Territories, the land north of Kowloon and over two hundred islands, to Britain for 99 years.

Britain wanted room to defend the harbour in a time when the European powers were seizing ports across a weak Qing China. The lease multiplied the colony's size many times. Villagers resisted at first, in a short war in 1899. A small fort inside the territory, Kowloon Walled City, was left under Chinese claim, and later became the lawless Walled City.

Most of Hong Kong's land, water and later its new towns lay in the New Territories, and the lease ran out in 1997. With no way to keep them, Britain opened the talks that led to the Joint Declaration and the return of the whole colony to China.
sum: The Convention for the Extension of Hong Kong Territory, signed in Beijing on 9 June 1898, leased the New Territories, the land north of Kowloon and over two hundred islands, to Britain for 99 years.
